newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels deny Angolan help as Kinshasa battle looms.
newsitem.headline: Rebels deny Angolan help as Kinshasa battle looms.

text.p: Zaire's rebel alliance on Friday denied receiving military help from Angola, saying reporters who claimed to have seen Angolan troops in the city of Lubumbashi were suffering from a collective delusion.
Rebel foreign minister Bizima Karaha, a physician by profession, said the international media in rebel-held Lubumbashi must be hallucinating and urged them to trust his diagnosis.
"I am a doctor. In medicine there is something called delusion...a fixed, false belief," he said to laughter.
"If you have a fixed, false belief there is nothing I can do. But believe me, they're not here," he told a news conference.
The Zairean rebel army, fighting to oust President Mobutu Sese Seko and end 32 years of his dictatorial rule, is believed to be getting substantial help from some African states.
Karaha made a point of insisting that the war would only end when Mobutu relinquished power, and not before. If he did not, the rebels would advance on the capital, Kinshasa.

An Angolan government jet was parked at Lubumbashi's military-controlled airport on Friday and a group of half a dozen heavily armed Portuguese-speaking commandos in spotless camouflage kit put up for the night at the city's main hotel.
They wore no insignia, shoulder flashes or badges of rank but looked like crack troops in a bodyguard unit such as might accompany a senior government figure.
Angola, scene of Africa's longest civil war, is a battle- hardened country to the southwest of Zaire.

It could provide a close jump-off point for a rebel advance on the Zairean capital, less than 200 km (120 miles) from the border, providing the Angolan government gave its consent and collaborated in planning such a project.
The rebel alliance of Laurent Kabila does have visitors from other countries, justice minister Mwenze Kongolo said. "We have a lot of friends in this war, we have a lot of support."
But he said many languages were spoken in Lubumbashi's main hotel and asked whether the reporters had "seen the passports of the soldiers" they assumed were Angolan.

Rwanda and Uganda are thought to be providing significant military backing for the rebel effort to topple Mobutu and there is speculation that rebel forces which took Lubumbashi 10 days ago were allowed to move through Zambia. This was officially denied in Lusaka.
